class.name: RecommendedGraphics
class.brief_description: Graphics settings recommended for the computer the game runs on.

method.name: apply
method.description: Sets [param settings] (from [method get_settings]) on [param viewport]. Each key is the name of a [Viewport] property, except [code]directional_shadow_size[/code], which sets the size of the directional shadow atlas (see [method RenderingServer.directional_shadow_atlas_set_size]).

method.name: benchmark
method.description: Measures the tiers in the game as it is running, best first. For each tier, calls [param apply_tier] with the tier, waits for it to settle and times every frame for a few seconds. It stops at the first tier that draws nine frames in ten within [param target_fps] (to within 5%), or at [constant TIER_LOW]. Await the returned signal for the tier chosen, which is applied when it completes. Vertical sync and [member Engine.max_fps] are lifted while it measures (each frame, so a game applying a tier through its own settings doesn't put them back), so a display's refresh rate doesn't hide how fast a tier can go, and put back after. In a headset they stay: the headset paces the frames, and its refresh rate is the target to give. Runs while the game is paused, so it can run from a settings menu. Only one benchmark runs at a time.

method.name: get_settings
method.description: Returns the engine settings recommended for [param tier] on the screen, or in a headset when [param headset] is [code]true[/code]. The keys are [code]scaling_3d_mode[/code], [code]scaling_3d_scale[/code], [code]msaa_3d[/code], [code]screen_space_aa[/code], [code]use_taa[/code], [code]anisotropic_filtering_level[/code], [code]mesh_lod_threshold[/code] and [code]directional_shadow_size[/code]. Apply them with [method apply]. Each tier below [constant TIER_ULTRA] draws at most so many pixels, so it upscales further on larger screens; [constant TIER_HIGH] draws a 4K screen at full size and a 5K one at about 85%, [constant TIER_LOW] draws 1080p at 70% and 4K at about half. In a headset, the lower tiers limit the pixels drawn for each eye the same way. Where a tier upscales, it uses a temporal upscaler when it smooths with TAA and a spatial one otherwise: MetalFX where the device supports it, FSR elsewhere. With the Mobile renderer, which has no TAA or temporal upscaling, FXAA takes TAA's place. A headset never uses TAA (it smears as the head turns), so it smooths with MSAA.

method.name: get_tier
method.description: Returns the tier the graphics adapter suggests. It reads the generation and class from the adapter's name (an RTX 4070's generation 40 and class 70, an M4 Max's generation 4 and Max), so later generations get a sensible tier too. Laptop graphics sit a step lower than the desktop card of the same name. Adapters from families it doesn't recognize go by their type: discrete ones [constant TIER_MEDIUM], others [constant TIER_LOW]. It's a first guess for a first run; [method benchmark] measures it.

constants.constant: The best: everything at full size and quality.
High settings, drawing a 4K screen at full size.
Medium settings, for discrete graphics a few generations old.
